title: Final Consonant Doubled
summary: A word ending in a single consonant preceded by a single vowel doubles the consonant before a vowel suffix.

rules.description: One syllable words or words accented on the final syllable double the final consonant before a vowel suffix.
Words ending in L usually double before a suffix in Canadian/British English.

title: Silent E Dropped
summary: Words ending in silent E usually drop the E before a vowel suffix.

rules.description: Drop silent E before suffixes beginning with a vowel (-ing, -ed, -able, -ous).
Keep the E before suffixes beginning with a consonant (-ment, -ness, -ful, -ly).
Keep the E after soft C or G before suffixes beginning with A or O.

title: IE and EI
summary: Use I before E except after C, or when sounding like A as in 'neighbour' and 'weigh'.

rules.description: I before E: believe, achieve, field, piece.
E before I after C: receive, ceiling, deceive.
E before I when sounding like A: neighbour, weigh, vein.

title: Y Changed to I
summary: When a word ends in consonant + Y, change Y to I before adding a suffix (except -ing).

rules.description: Change Y to I before most suffixes: -es, -ed, -er, -est, -ful, -ness, -ly.
Keep the Y before -ing.
If a vowel comes before the Y, keep the Y.

title: Adding Prefixes
summary: When a prefix is added to a word, the spelling of the root word does not change.

rules.description: The spelling of the root word stays the same when a prefix is added.

title: Adding Suffixes -TION and -SION
summary: Words ending in -TION and -SION follow specific patterns.

rules.description: Use -TION after most consonants and long vowels.
Use -SION after L, N, R and after the letters S or D in the root word.
Most nouns: add -S.
Nouns ending in S, X, Z, CH, SH: add -ES.
Nouns ending in consonant + Y: change Y to I, add -ES.
Some nouns ending in F or FE: change to -VES.

title: Silent Letters
summary: Some words contain letters that are not pronounced.

rules.description: Common silent letters: K in KN (know, knee), W in WR (write, wrong), B in MB (comb, climb).
Silent GH in words like caught, daughter, thought.

title: Homophones
summary: Words that sound the same but have different spellings and meanings.

rules.description: In a spelling bee, the pronouncer will always provide the definition and an example sentence for homophones.
Always listen carefully to the definition to determine the correct spelling.

title: Canadian Spelling
summary: Canadian English follows British spelling conventions for certain patterns.

rules.description: Use -OUR instead of -OR: colour, honour, neighbour, favourite.
Use -RE instead of -ER: centre, theatre, metre, litre.
Double L before suffixes: travelling, cancellation, labelling.
